newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany extradites Iran murder suspect to France.
newsitem.headline: Germany extradites Iran murder suspect to France.

text.p: Germany has extradited to France an Iranian wanted in connection with the killing of former Iranian minister Reza Mazlouman in Paris last May, prosecutors said on Friday.

Bonn resident Ahmad Jeyhouni was flown out late on Thursday after a high court ruled Paris's extradition request was valid and the federal government approved the deportation, a spokesman for the Cologne prosecutor's office said.

Jeyhouni, 61, is wanted on suspicion of taking part in the killing of Mazlouman, a vice-minister of education under the late Shah before the 1979 Islamic revolution, and was arrested in Bonn last May at France's request.
Jeyhouni had contested his extradition but failed to persuade the court that evidence he produced constituted an impediment to his return to France.
French media say Jeyhouni ran a video cassette shop in Bonn, and that he had been identified by a woman friend of Mazlouman as having visited him just before the killing.

The French investigation is being led by anti-terrorism judge Jean-Louis Bruguiere, who investigated the murder of the shah's last prime minister, Shapour Bakhtiar, in France in 1991. Several Iranians were convicted of the murder two years ago.
Since the 1979 revolution, eight Iranian exiles have been killed in France and several dozen in other countries.

Iranian resistance officials say Tehran was behind the murders, and allege that the Iranian embassy in Bonn houses a coordination centre for attacks on dissidents living in Europe. Iran has always denied involvement in such attacks.
